clue.text: When time stood still at Grantchester

definitions.text: When time stood still at Grantchester

parts.words: When time stood still at Grantchester
parts.note: Rupert Brooke's poem about the Cambridgeshire village of Grantchester asks whether its church clock still stands at a certain hour

explanation.walkthrough: The line is from Rupert Brooke's 'The Old Vicarage, Grantchester': 'Stands the Church clock at ten to three? And is there honey still for tea?' Grantchester is a village outside Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: In Brooke's poem the church clock is imagined stopped forever at this hour, the moment the village's timelessness is pinned to.

clue.text: Run out with tenpence into the republic

indicators.note: into puts the money inside the name of the republic

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for the Republic of Ireland
X is the Roman numeral ten and P stands for pence

explanation.surface: Someone flees to Ireland with only ten pence to their name.
explanation.definitionFit: When a passport or licence runs out it comes to an end and is no longer valid.

clue.text: Seaside device for running in three-legged race, say?

indicators.note: say tells us the phrase is to be spoken and heard as another

parts.note: in a three-legged race two runners are bound at the ankle, so their running is a tied gait

explanation.surface: A beach gadget meant for a sports-day race where partners run with legs bound together.
explanation.walkthrough: A three-legged race is a school sports-day event where pairs run with adjacent legs tied together.
explanation.definitionFit: A tide gate is a sluice on the coast that lets water flow with the tide in one direction only.

clue.text: With which gipsy accompanies a doctor in tour in the Orient

indicators.note: in puts the article and the doctor inside the word tour

parts.note: taken as written
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, a medical degree
taken as written
E for east, the Orient

explanation.surface: A Romany musician plays along on a doctor's trip round the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' (the first) puts A and MB inside TOUR, giving TAMBOUR; IN and E follow.
explanation.definitionFit: The small hand drum with jingles is the instrument traditionally associated with Romany dancers and players.

clue.text: Mrs Beeton gave you more than one for your money

definitions.text: Mrs Beeton gave you more than one

explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Beeton was a Victorian writer of a famous British cookery and household-management book.
explanation.definitionFit: In old usage a receipt was a recipe, and Mrs Beeton's famous household book gave hundreds; today it is the slip you get when you pay.

clue.text: Advantage of brinkmanship

explanation.definitionFit: An edge is a slight lead over rivals; and brinkmanship is pushing a dispute to the brink, the very lip of disaster.

clue.text: Puts in a pound to arrange the wedding

indicators.note: to arrange means these letters are reordered into a new word

parts.note: L, from libra, is the abbreviation for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: Someone stumps up a pound to organise a marriage ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuptials is a formal word for a marriage ceremony.

clue.text: What the agent does about the gifts

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
presents are gifts

explanation.surface: An agent is asked what they do about the presents.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent acts on behalf of a client, standing in for them.

clue.text: Appoint as (a French) representative

explanation.surface: Someone is being appointed to act on behalf of the French.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket hints that the second reading belongs to French: un député is an elected deputy.
explanation.definitionFit: To depute is to delegate or appoint an agent; and in France a député is a member of the National Assembly, a representative.

clue.text: Popular complaint is the same in Latin, in poetry

indicators.note: the second in places one piece within the other, the Latin word sitting inside the poetry

parts.note: an epic is a long heroic poem, standing for poetry
idem is the Latin for the same, familiar from footnotes

explanation.surface: A poet observes that a widespread illness is described identically in Latin verse.
explanation.definitionFit: An outbreak of disease affecting many people at once is a complaint shared by the populace, hence popular.

clue.text: Oriental tax in part reversed — brings us to another story

indicators.note: in tells us the eastern tax goes inside the turned-round part
reversed tells us the word for part is read backwards

parts.note: a role is an actor's part
E for east, the Orient
VAT, value added tax, the British sales tax

explanation.surface: An eastern levy is partly turned back, a twist that takes the tale somewhere new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' turns ROLE into ELOR, and 'in' puts E and VAT inside it. 'story' is the floor of a building (British 'storey'), not a tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A lift carries passengers between floors, a storey being one level of a building.

clue.text: In Greece a letter from the heart, say ?

indicators.note: say tells us to speak the word for the heart and hear another

parts.note: the heart is a beater, the organ that beats

explanation.surface: A love letter from someone in Greece, straight from the heart.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent BEATER and BETA sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: The second character of the Greek alphabet, following alpha.

clue.text: Charley's aunt's cracked compatriots

parts.note: in the farce Charley's Aunt the aunt is said to come from a South American country where certain nuts come from, so her compatriots are nuts to be cracked

explanation.walkthrough: Brandon Thomas's Victorian farce has the line 'I'm Charley's aunt from Brazil, where the nuts come from'. 'cracked' suggests mad, but here the nuts are opened.
explanation.definitionFit: Large hard-shelled seeds from a South American tree, shelled with a nutcracker, are the aunt's countrymen in the play's joke.

clue.text: Socially on top, but in the middle

definitions.text: Socially on top, but in the middle

parts.words: Socially on top, but in the middle
parts.note: the social elite are at the top, yet the same phrase names the higher form in a school, which may sit in the middle of the building or the year groups

explanation.definitionFit: The aristocratic tier sits highest in the social hierarchy, while a school's senior form is a higher grade, not necessarily the top one.

clue.text: This man finds his post lucrative

definitions.text: This man finds his post lucrative

parts.words: This man finds his post lucrative
parts.note: post seems to be a job, but it is the mail that brings this man money sent from home

explanation.walkthrough: A remittance man was an Englishman paid by his family to live abroad and stay out of the way; his income arrived by mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Money sent by post to such an exile is a payment remitted, which is what his title names.

clue.text: Country that's half-German inter alia

indicators.note: inter is the Latin for among or between, so the piece is put among the letters of alia

parts.note: taken as written, from the Latin phrase inter alia, among other things

indicators.note: half takes the first three of the six letters of German

explanation.surface: A nation that is, among other things, partly German.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin phrase 'inter alia' (among other things) is split: 'inter' puts GER, half of GERMAN, among the letters ALIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A North African nation whose capital is Algiers.

clue.text: Agreed — an unruly sort of swine

indicators.note: unruly means the letters are out of order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Everyone agrees: here is a badly behaved pig.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Gospels, Jesus sends demons into the Gadarene swine, which rush headlong into the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical herd of pigs possessed by demons gives a name for a reckless headlong rush.

clue.text: Person loses his head about me as a poet

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word me is read backwards
losing the head means the first letter of the word person is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone decapitated near me, as a poet might describe it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson was an American essayist and poet of the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Repeat crime ? Send back to prison

explanation.definitionFit: To commit an offence again is to perpetrate it a second time; and a court may return a prisoner to jail by a further committal.

clue.text: A farcical situation in any household

definitions.text: A farcical situation in any household

parts.words: A farcical situation in any household
parts.note: situation means location: the room where stage farces with their hiding lovers are set, found in every home

explanation.walkthrough: A bedroom farce is a British stage comedy of mistaken identity and illicit liaisons.
explanation.definitionFit: The room for sleeping is where the comic genre of farce stages its trousers-down confusions.

clue.text: Attraction of the French building material in the beginning

indicators.note: the beginning says the word in stands at the front of the answer

parts.note: taken as written
du is French for of the
cement binds bricks and stone

explanation.surface: The appeal of French construction materials from the very start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the beginning' puts IN at the front, ahead of DU and CEMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An incentive or lure that draws someone to act is an attraction.

clue.text: River's projections

explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe is kept in the first reading: the Cam's, belonging to the river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cam is the river through Cambridge, so the river's is Cam's; and cams are projections on a rotating shaft that drive machinery.

clue.text: Wherewith Messrs French, bagging an antelope, celebrate ?

definitions.text: Wherewith Messrs French, bagging an antelope, celebrate

indicators.note: bagging means capturing, so the two letters hold the others inside them

parts.note: MM is the abbreviation of Messieurs, French for Messrs
a gnu is an African antelope, the wildebeest

explanation.surface: Two French gentlemen shoot an antelope and toast the kill.
explanation.walkthrough: The hunters 'bag' a gnu and celebrate with a big bottle of champagne.
explanation.definitionFit: A double-size champagne bottle is what hunters might crack open to celebrate their bag.

clue.text: Man with relations

parts.note: relations looks like family, but a relation is also an account or story told, so this is a man who tells tales

explanation.definitionFit: A storyteller gives an account, and to relate a story is to tell it.

clue.text: Nips will grow into nippers

explanation.surface: Little drinks that grow up to be children.
explanation.definitionFit: A tot is a small measure of spirits, a nip; and tots are also small children, nippers.

clue.text: "A lovely apparition sent To be a moment's —" (Wordsworth)

definitions.text: "A lovely apparition sent To be a moment's —" (Wordsworth)

parts.words: "A lovely apparition sent To be a moment's —" (Wordsworth)
parts.note: the missing word completes a line of Wordsworth's 'She was a Phantom of delight', rhyming with moment

explanation.walkthrough: Wordsworth's poem runs 'A lovely Apparition, sent / To be a moment's ornament'.
explanation.definitionFit: The woman of the poem is a brief decoration to the moment, an adornment.

clue.text: Can trophy be so cheaply made?

parts.note: a tin is a can
a pot is slang for a sporting trophy or cup

explanation.surface: A question whether a cup could be manufactured on the cheap.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinpot means shoddy, inferior or second-rate, like something made for very little money.

clue.text: Period of horological advancement

parts.note: horological means to do with clocks; the period is the season when clocks are put forward an hour

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain clocks go forward an hour in spring and back in autumn; the months between are known by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Daylight saving time, the months when the clocks have been moved forward an hour.
